result:
The de-duplication was reworked in PR #3374, a follow-up to #3345. The root cause is that `/obstree` returns the same observation under several branches (Bloodwork contains Hematology, and each root carries a full copy of the obs list). Keying on `flatName` and concatenating copies showed one Platelets result as two. The fix treats whole obs lists as the unit of de-duplication:

- **`filter-reducer.ts`** merges same-`flatName` duplicates with a multiset union, keeping the highest count of each `obsDatetime|value` seen in any single branch, instead of concatenating. It also copies nodes rather than mutating the SWR-cached trees. (`mergeObsMultisetMax` at lines 11–39.)
- **`filter-context.tsx`** builds a normalized branch list keyed by rendered panel plus `conceptUuid` (via `deriveGroupKey`). Duplicate branches are collapsed with the same merge. `tableData`, `timelineData`, and both result counts all derive from this list, so the header count matches the rows. (Lines 39–47 and 113–132.)
- **`tree-view` and `grouped-timeline`** match checkbox filters against all contributing `flatNames`, so filtering by either alias of a collapsed branch keeps its row visible.

Two things it does not solve: `obsDatetime + value` still cannot tell a copy from two real results with the same value and time, and that limitation is documented in the code. The fix for that is server-side. The PR's "Other" section proposes adding obs `uuid` to the obstree response (`ObsTreeResource1_9` in the REST module), which would make de-duplication exact. That became ticket **RESTWS-1038**, per a comment from denniskigen. REST PR #751, "RESTWS-1038: Include obs uuid in the obstree response", is open and references it. I did not confirm the ticket in Jira itself.

The change that answers the question is PR #3374 (merge commit `d47d346`). The earlier PR #3345 (merge commit `16600fb`) switched the key from `flatName` to `conceptUuid`, which was the first step and is what #3374 corrects for the Hematology/Bloodwork overlap.
